title: Orot HaKodesh
text: The active wisdom of the holy. Wisdom of the holy is exalted above all wisdom, in that it overturns the will and spiritual-mental attribute of those that learn it to bring them closer to the very elevation by which it itself is intensified. This is not so regarding all other worldly wisdoms, for even though they draw from sublime, beautiful and noble ideas, they do not have this active attribute - to extend the very self-essence of their ponderer toward their values - and in truth each of them has no relationship whatsoever to other forces or the human self except for the force of its own discipline alone. And the reason for this is that all holy ideas come from the life-source of the living, from the life-foundation of all existence, and in them is the holy content to constitute multitudes of creations without end, to establish the heavens and form the earth, and all the more so to embed a new form and to imprint it on the soul of their ponderer. And no secular knowledges contain this power, because they are not self-renewing nor do they generate newness themselves, but they depict and display what is found in reality from the viewpoint of the intellect, and therefore they are not also able to make their ponderer into a new creation, to uproot him from his evil attributes and place him in the situation of a new reality, pure and alive in the light of true life, which stands forever.

10. Love Without Cause and Hatred Without Cause - Understanding and imagination, knowledge and will — are these not merely small sparks from the treasury of life? The treasury itself is filled with an unsearchable fullness, in an awesome depth. The fierce vitality of life, which discloses itself in the will-to-live — and of which all particular desires are the offspring — is exceedingly strong in its fortitude. Its form is fixed; all spiritual forms are struck according to that same die which lies hidden deep within it. When strife breaks out between one force and another, between one person and another, between one nation and another, between one world and another — the strife, in its inner content, is an outcome of the differentiation and opposition present within the very essence of the treasury of life. Very slight is the worth of those grounds of opposition that get articulated in reasoned understanding and scientific specification; all of these are faint markers, which, owing to the weakness of our cognition, present themselves as though they were causes and claims. But the supreme foundation is hatred without cause — that which the treasury of life expresses toward whatever stands opposed to it. And this drive of hatred-without-cause enfolds within itself the hidden recess of love, which is likewise, in equal measure, love without cause; and in it alone lies stored the light of peace and of happiness. All the reasonings that appear in logical disclosure and in an ordered, delineated scheme are only faint sparks. For since the bounded sphere of the human being's present standing in life cannot receive the exaltation of that treasury's light in the fullness of its inwardness, one makes do with thin conceptions, which contain only dark shadows of that primordiality belonging to love-without-cause and hatred-without-cause, whose foundation is hate evil and love good. And inasmuch as the depth of evil and the loftiness of its root is in truth the depth of good, it follows that the depth of hatred is in truth the depth of love. And if we were destroyed, and the world with us, through hatred without cause — we shall return to be rebuilt, and the world with us, through love without cause, which descends from the top of the rocks: and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy — which is the faithful vision of the passing of all the good before his face, of that man Moses. But at once, at his birth, the good came with him: and she saw him, that he was good — let the good one come and receive good from the Good One for the good ones.

11. Looking upon the Good Side - When one looks truly at the good side of each and every person, he becomes beloved among people with an inward affection, and has no need to resort to any particle of flattery. For the attentiveness to the good side, which he encounters constantly, genuinely conceals from him all the bad sides — and the prudent one covers over disgrace.
